//: Markup-fidelity fixture for the SIDEBAR shell — the `.pc-layout__sidebar` block (keen `PureAdmin.Components.Layout.sidebar/1`, svelte `layout/Sidebar.svelte`). A SHELL component migrated DOWN into @keenmate/pure-css, so the block class is `pc-layout__sidebar` (NOT `pa-sidebar`); confirmed in dist/css/main.css. SCOPE = CAPABILITY-ONLY, ZERO strict-compare scenarios — same path as navbar.json / settings-panel.json / command-palette.json, because the two wrappers' PRE-JS-hook SSR shells are IRRECONCILABLE on the root element both ALWAYS emit, `<aside class="pc-layout__sidebar">`: keen stamps it with `phx-hook="PureAdminSidebar"` (stripped by the normalizer, fine) AND a DEFAULT `id="sidebar"` (the sidebar hook's anchor — toggle_sidebar(id) / drag-resize target it), while svelte (a reactive component, no `id` prop) emits a BARE `<aside class="pc-layout__sidebar">` with no id. The normalizer KEEPS `id` (see navbar.json / normalize.mjs), so keen's `id="sidebar"` survives and can never equal svelte's absent id. Crucially the id is NOT in the oracle snippet (packages/core/snippets/layout.html shows `<aside class="pc-layout__sidebar">` with no id) — it is keen-specific hook plumbing, so FORCING svelte to grow a matching `id` prop would gold-plate an un-blessed attribute (unlike modal, whose root id IS in the snippet because openModal(id) targets it). A shared golden therefore can't write the `<aside>` opening tag. Everything INSIDE — the `pc-sidebar__*` BEM family (section/divider/item/link/toggle/icon/label/chevron/submenu/search) — is a SEPARATE block fed through the slot by sub-components (keen sidebar_item/sidebar_submenu/sidebar_section/sidebar_divider/sidebar_search; svelte SidebarItem/…), out of scope here (container-only), and NOT matched by the ^pc-layout__sidebar axis regexes anyway. Because there is no shared full-tree golden, compare passes vacuously (0/0 both wrappers) and correctness is asserted by the completeness contract: the base `pc-layout__sidebar` class + its one REAL CSS block modifier (--icon-collapse, prop-driven, emitted identically by both wrappers → modeled as a feature) + the prop-driven --resizable JS activation marker (a class token with zero SCSS rules → produces:null, like modal's `static`) + the lone `pc-layout__sidebar__nav` element + the shared class passthrough. Canonical shape: packages/core/snippets/layout.html (SIDEBAR sections).

propsVocabulary.iconCollapse: boolean — collapse to an icon rail; emits pc-layout__sidebar--icon-collapse. svelte `isIconCollapse`, keen `is_icon_collapse`. The ONLY visual sidebar-element modifier.
propsVocabulary.resizable: boolean — opt into core's drag-to-resize driver; emits pc-layout__sidebar--resizable (a JS activation marker, no SCSS rules of its own). svelte `isResizable`, keen `is_resizable`. The driver injects the .pc-sidebar-resize handle at RUNTIME — never in SSR markup (both wrappers deliberately render no handle).
propsVocabulary.extraClass: extra classes appended verbatim to the root <aside class="pc-layout__sidebar ..."> (svelte `class`, keen `class`) — class passthrough; not a core modifier.

goldenConventions: No scenarios → no goldens. See the leading note for why a shared full-tree golden is impossible: the always-present root `<aside>` carries keen's default hook-anchor id (toggle/resize target) that svelte doesn't emit, and the id is NOT in the oracle snippet so svelte should not grow a matching prop. The two block modifiers (--icon-collapse / --resizable) ARE prop-driven and emitted identically by both wrappers, so they are modeled as features for the completeness axes even though no strict scenario can assert them (the root can't reconcile). The resize HANDLE (.pc-sidebar-resize*) is JS-built at runtime, never SSR — not part of this contract (and not a pc-layout__sidebar__* element). Attribute + class-token order and whitespace would be normalized away if a golden existed.

features.//: Feature→class contract authored from dist/css/main.css (grep '\.pc-layout__sidebar'). Block modifiers: --icon-collapse + --resizable (both prop-driven, both wrappers → features). Element classes under ^pc-layout__sidebar__: only `pc-layout__sidebar__nav` (the <nav> wrapper the container emits around the <ul>). The whole `pc-sidebar__*` BEM family is a DIFFERENT block (pc-sidebar, note the single `__` segment after pc-sidebar not after pc-layout__sidebar) fed by slot sub-components → not matched by the axis regexes, covered by their own future slices. `.pc-sidebar-resize*` / `.pc-sidebar-resizing` / `.pc-sidebar-resized` are also separate blocks (JS-built handle + body state), out of this block's surface.

iconCollapse.note: svelte isIconCollapse, keen is_icon_collapse. The one visual sidebar modifier. Modeled as a feature (axis-1/2); not strict-compared (root can't reconcile — see note).

resizable.note: svelte isResizable, keen is_resizable. Emits the class token `pc-layout__sidebar--resizable` on the element, but that class is a pure JS ACTIVATION MARKER with ZERO SCSS rules (confirmed absent from dist/css/main.css — grep '\.pc-layout__sidebar--resizable' is empty; the shipped sidebar-resize driver keys off it to pick which sidebar to wire and inject the .pc-sidebar-resize handle at runtime). So `produces: null` (like modal's `static`): it's a declared, mapped feature but produces no CSS-backed modifier, hence not subject to the axis-1 PHANTOM/UNMAPPED checks. Not strict-compared (root can't reconcile).

extraClass.note: class passthrough — appended verbatim to the root pc-layout__sidebar aside; svelte `class`, keen `class`. Declared in both maps for axis-2.

deferred.//: The one element class under ^pc-layout__sidebar__ is `pc-layout__sidebar__nav`, emitted by the container shell around the slotted <ul>. It IS in both wrappers' SSR identically, but it can't be strict-compared because the root <aside> it nests under carries keen's hook-anchor id (see leading note); acknowledged as PROSE. (The whole pc-sidebar__* BEM family — items/links/sections/etc. — belongs to the SEPARATE `pc-sidebar` block fed by slot sub-components and is NOT matched by this block's ^pc-layout__sidebar__ regex, so it needs no entry here; it is covered by its own future sub-component slices.)
deferred.pc-layout__sidebar__nav: the <nav> wrapper the container emits around the sidebar <ul>. Both wrappers emit `<nav class="pc-sidebar__nav">` here — but note main.css ALSO carries a `.pc-layout__sidebar__nav` selector (a BEM-nested alias of the same wrapper); it is container chrome, deferred because the root it sits under can't reconcile.
